research.text: My research integrates clinical data, medical imaging, artificial intelligence and quantitative biomarkers to investigate neurological disease, occupational lung disease and cancer. Working with clinical and research teams, I connect clinically meaningful questions with study design, data collection, analysis and validation to generate evidence for diagnosis, disease characterisation and clinical decision-making.

research.title: Epilepsy: lesion detection and segmentation
research.question: How can MRI and machine learning help detect and delineate subtle brain abnormalities associated with focal epilepsy?
research.contribution: I develop unsupervised lesion-detection methods for 7T MRI and multimodal segmentation methods using T1-weighted and FLAIR images, with a focus on focal cortical dysplasia, small lesions and model failures.

research.title: Predicting seizure recurrence after a first seizure
research.question: Can clinical information and MRI-derived brain measurements help estimate the likelihood of another seizure?
research.contribution: I develop imaging features and machine-learning methods, integrate clinical information, and evaluate predictive performance. This includes NeuroMorphix, which captures brain asymmetry from structural MRI.

research.title: Alzheimer’s disease: structural MRI biomarkers
research.question: How can structural MRI characterise brain changes across normal cognition, mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer’s disease?
research.contribution: I analyse cortical and subcortical measurements and networks describing similarities between brain regions, combining machine learning with harmonisation across imaging sites to investigate potential biomarkers.

research.title: Friedreich’s ataxia: diffusion MRI and cerebellar pathways
research.question: How can diffusion MRI quantify changes in the cerebellar pathways affected by Friedreich’s ataxia?
research.contribution: I develop automated methods to segment the cerebellar peduncles and extract measurements of white matter microstructure, evaluating segmentation accuracy and consistency across imaging sites.

research.title: Chest X-ray and CT assessment in dust-exposed workers
research.question: How closely does chest X-ray assessment agree with high-resolution CT (HRCT), and how well does it identify abnormalities in dust-exposed workers?
research.contribution: At I-MED Radiology Network, I lead research delivery and analysis in occupational lung imaging. ExactDust examines agreement and diagnostic performance between chest radiography and HRCT, alongside related work on quantitative assessment of structural lung abnormalities.

research.title: Linking quantitative CT with lung function
research.question: How do quantitative CT measurements relate to spirometry and other measures of lung function in coal mine dust lung disease?
research.contribution: In ACARP-supported research, I evaluate CT-derived measurements against spirometry and other available pulmonary function measures to investigate relationships between lung structure and function.

research.title: PET–CT tumour segmentation across cancer types
research.question: How well do PET–CT tumour segmentation models generalise across cancer types and patient cohorts?
research.contribution: I evaluate nnU-Net across oesophageal and lung cancer cohorts and public datasets, comparing training strategies and analysing segmentation errors.

about.text: I am a clinical data and medical imaging AI researcher based in Brisbane, Australia. My work brings together clinical records, structural and diffusion MRI, quantitative CT and machine learning to investigate neurological disease, occupational lung disease and cancer. I work with clinical and research teams across study design, data preparation, method development and evaluation.

Senior Researcher · I-MED Radiology Network
Clinical AI evaluation, quantitative imaging and occupational lung disease research.

Honorary Fellow · The University of Queensland
Neuroimaging and medical imaging AI research.

Adjunct Lecturer · Charles Darwin University
Appointed September 2026.

I completed my PhD in machine learning and neuroimaging at The University of Queensland in 2024, supervised by Professor David Reutens and Associate Professor Viktor Vegh. My doctoral research focused on MRI and machine learning in epilepsy.

My previous research appointments include QIMR Berghofer’s Cerebellum & Neurodegeneration Research Group, UQ’s Centre for Advanced Imaging, and a visiting research role with RBWH Neurology. Earlier research experience at IIIT Sri City and the University of Hyderabad established my foundations in machine learning and feature selection.
Education: PhD, The University of Queensland (2024); M.Tech in Information Technology, University of Hyderabad (2016); MCA (2013) and BCA (2010), West Bengal University of Technology.
PReMI–Springer Student Award (2017) · MICCAI Student Participation Award (2021) · UQ HDR travel support to attend AES (2023).
Academic service includes reviewing for ML4H and programme committee contributions to the ICCV CVAMD workshop.
For collaboration enquiries or supervision discussions, contact soumen.ghosh@uq.edu.au.

teaching.text: I teach across machine learning, data science and mathematical foundations, and supervise student research in medical image analysis. My approach connects conceptual understanding with reproducible experiments, careful evaluation and clear scientific communication.

The University of Queensland
Teaching and tutoring in Introduction to Data Science (DATA7001), Digital Health Software Project (COMP3820) and Research Methods (ENGG7811).

James Cook University, Brisbane — previous appointment
Sessional Lecturer in MA2011 Discrete Mathematics.

Sessional Lecturer in TECH3100: Data Visualization in R.

IIIT Sri City and University of Hyderabad
Earlier teaching support in deep learning, machine learning, statistics, discrete mathematics, probability and R programming.
I supervise undergraduate and postgraduate students on research projects in medical imaging AI, including the development of a shared brain MRI lesion segmentation pipeline.
Projects emphasise data quality, preprocessing, reproducible training, meaningful baselines, lesion-level evaluation and failure analysis.

Brain MRI lesion detection and segmentation

Structural and diffusion MRI biomarkers

Quantitative thoracic imaging

Robustness and clinical evaluation of imaging AI
Students interested in research projects, internships or remotely supervised work are welcome to contact me with a brief description of their interests and experience.
I also deliver the Clinical AI course and tailored workshops for research and industry teams.

research_delivery.title: Research Design and Delivery
research_delivery.intro: My experience spans the design and delivery of research involving clinical data, medical imaging and artificial intelligence. Working with clinical and research teams, I connect study planning, ethics and hospital coordination with data collection, reference standards, analytical methods, validation and scientific reporting.

capabilities.title: Study Design and Planning
capabilities.text: Defining clinical research questions, study objectives, patient eligibility criteria, outcome measures and analysis plans.

capabilities.title: Ethics and Study Coordination
capabilities.text: Preparing ethics documentation, supporting research governance, coordinating patient recruitment and working with hospital and research teams.

capabilities.title: Clinical Data and Reference Standards
capabilities.text: Collecting and linking clinical records and images from hospital systems (eMR/PACS), de-identifying and preparing data, and establishing reference standards with clinical experts.

capabilities.title: Analysis and Model Development
capabilities.text: Statistical analysis, image preprocessing, feature engineering, quantitative biomarker development and machine learning using clinical data and medical images.

capabilities.title: Validation and Clinical Interpretation
capabilities.text: Evaluating predictive and segmentation performance, testing generalisability across cohorts, investigating errors and interpreting findings with clinical collaborators.

capabilities.title: Reporting and Reproducibility
capabilities.text: Preparing research reports, manuscripts and conference presentations, supported by documented methods, reproducible analysis workflows and clear reporting of limitations.
